items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: she made me get involved in everything in junior high school

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Certainly they did. Everything I did -- and I think that musically, in junior high school it was better for me for music than high school, actually, because that's where I learned to conduct, really, in junior high school.

Because I had a teacher, her name was Ms. Goodrich, and she was a wonderful lady and a good musician, and she made me get involved in everything in junior high school, you know, musically? That was when I was in the glee club and I was in the dramatic class; I played Penrod and Penrod and Sam, and she was quite -- she had quite an influence on me, because she went to Jefferson High School. She transferred and went to Jefferson High School, and when I finished Lafayette, I went to Jefferson High School at first,…

That was an experience that I didn't realize, you know, because in later years, when I started conducting for Nat, it finally dawned on me, you know, why I picked it up so fast. I had forgotten that I had done it, you know, because we played all legitimate music in junior high school. You know, you played all the semi classics, you know, kind of heavy music you played ... symphony. And she used to --
